stem: Which scenario is least consistent with risky sexual behaviour in an adolescent health assessment?

options.text: A young person has sexual intercourse at an early age without protection
A young person has several partners over a short period and uses condoms inconsistently
A young person has sex that affects their mental health and gives no pleasure
A young person has sexual behaviour that increases the risk of STI or unplanned pregnancy
A young person has consensual sex with condom or contraceptive use and no reported wellbeing impact

explanation: Consensual sex with condom or contraceptive use and no reported wellbeing impact is least consistent with risky sexual behaviour. Risky sexual behaviour includes early sexual debut, multiple partners over a short period, inconsistent condom or contraceptive use, and sexual activity associated with STI or unplanned pregnancy risk or reduced wellbeing.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because early sexual intercourse without protection is a recognised marker of risky sexual behaviour.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because multiple partners over a short period with inconsistent condom use increases STI and pregnancy risk.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because sexual activity affecting mental health and giving no pleasure is consistent with wellbeing harm.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because increased risk of STI or unplanned pregnancy is part of the definition of risky sexual behaviour.
optionExplanations.E: Correct because consensual sex with condom or contraceptive use and no reported wellbeing impact is the least consistent with risky sexual behaviour.
